[d/g2074788f713e-1] decision (cited, source git:2074788f713ef4331ede63d3dc963f8e74e7565c)
  Route all time readings through a process-wide session clock.
  The system clock can step backwards due to NTP, VM resume, or operator; a continuously running wallclock would show time going backward. The session clock ensures one monotonic reading order.

[d/g2074788f713e-11] decision (cited, source crates/ucal/src/clock.rs@2074788f713e)
  Ignore poison on the session mutex and take the inner value.

[d/g2074788f713e-2] decision (cited, source git:2074788f713ef4331ede63d3dc963f8e74e7565c)
  Use max(wall_now, anchor + monotonic_elapsed) as the reading rule.
  Backward steps lose to monotonic branch to keep advancing; forward steps win to track system corrections.

[d/g2074788f713e-4] decision (cited, source crates/ucal/src/clock.rs@2074788f713e)
  Make Session::reading a pure function of its inputs.

[d/g2074788f713e-6] decision (cited, source git:2074788f713ef4331ede63d3dc963f8e74e7565c)
  Store session state as Option and anchor lazily inside session_now, avoiding .expect.
  OnceLock's initializer cannot return a Result; no-panic-in-cli lint refused .expect. Option allows anchoring where a failure can be returned.

[d/g2074788f713e-7] decision (cited, source git:2074788f713ef4331ede63d3dc963f8e74e7565c)
  Split wall_instant out of now_instant to expose a raw system clock reading.
  now_instant goes through session clock; doctor --clock and measurements need the raw reading. Splitting also exposed the feature gate issue.

[d/g2074788f713e-8] decision (cited, source git:2074788f713ef4331ede63d3dc963f8e74e7565c)
  Gate wall_instant (and session clock) under the civil feature.
  Converting a clock reading is a leap-table lookup, because Unix time is a UTC label. The feature workflow caught the missing gate when building with u512,std.

[d/g21665b3aac9b-1] decision (cited, source git:21665b3aac9be9a762eada806b9ccb56c3cbabea)

[p/g2074788f713e-2-1] constraint (cited, source crates/ucal/src/clock.rs@2074788f713e)

[p/g2074788f713e-2-2] constraint (cited, source crates/ucal/src/clock.rs@2074788f713e)

[r/g2074788f713e-1-1] claim (cited, source git:2074788f713ef4331ede63d3dc963f8e74e7565c)
  Rejected: Let each wallclock tick read the raw system clock directly.
  A backward step would produce a face that goes back in time.
  -> contrasts d/g2074788f713e-1

[r/g2074788f713e-11-1] claim (cited, source crates/ucal/src/clock.rs@2074788f713e)
  Rejected: Propagate the poison error from `session().lock()`.
  The state is a pair of tick counts and cannot be torn, so taking the inner value is correct.
  -> contrasts d/g2074788f713e-11

[r/g2074788f713e-4-1] claim (cited, source crates/ucal/src/clock.rs@2074788f713e)
  Rejected: Have Session::reading read the wall clock itself.
  A pure function lets tests drive a wall clock backwards and assert the answer does not follow.
  -> contrasts d/g2074788f713e-4

[r/g2074788f713e-6-2] claim (cited, source crates/ucal/src/clock.rs@2074788f713e)
  Rejected: Anchor the session at process start-up.
  A command that never asks the time should not read a clock, and most do not.
  -> contrasts d/g2074788f713e-6

[r/g449b762e3cca-10-1] claim (cited, source Documentation/CLI.md@449b762e3cca)
  Rejected: Allow the inverse for calendars with no anchor.
  The same error as the forward direction, UCAL-E0062, applies; thirteen of fifteen derived calendars are in this state.
  -> contrasts d/g449b762e3cca-10
